trigger_evals.prompt: Create a GitHub epic for the billing rewrite and organize the existing issues underneath it.
Open a parent initiative for migrating authentication across the web app, API, and workers.
Turn this roadmap item into a delivery-ready epic with child workstreams and dependencies.
Use gh to create an Epic issue, attach #120 and #121 as sub-issues, and mark it blocked by #88.
Create a GitLab epic for the observability program with inherited dates and existing child issues.
Refine this epic so its goals, non-goals, success criteria, risks, and child hierarchy are complete.
Decompose this initiative into child issues and nested epics without duplicating existing work.
Draft an epic for the checkout redesign but do not create anything remotely yet.
Set the roadmap project, Golden Pounds, target date, and health metadata on this epic.
Move these existing issues under the payments epic and preserve their blocker relationships.
Create an umbrella issue that tracks the multi-service PostgreSQL migration as native sub-issues.
Split this large feature into two epics because it has separate outcomes and release paths.
Create a single implementation-ready issue for fixing the login timeout.
Write a conventional commit message for these staged files.
Create a pull request for the current branch.
Summarize epic #42 without changing it.
Review this roadmap and tell me which initiative is highest priority.
Create a release milestone for version 3.0.
Explain how GitHub sub-issues work.
List all epics currently at risk.
Generate Vitest tests for this Vue component.
Implement all issues in epic #91.
Close every completed child issue in this epic.
Create a project board for our Q4 roadmap.

output_evals.prompt: Create a GitHub epic for the session-platform migration. The org already has an Epic issue type, Roadmap project, Priority, Golden Pounds, and Target date fields. Reuse #120 and #121 as children, create missing deliverables, and mark the epic blocked by #88.
assertions: Inspects repository conventions, existing Epic issue type, fields, project, and overlapping work before creation.
Produces a coherent outcome with goals, non-goals, scope, success signals, workstreams, sequencing, risks, rollout, and epic-level acceptance criteria.
Reuses #120 and #121 rather than duplicating them.
Uses native sub-issue and blocked-by relationships instead of only Markdown links.
Uses the existing Epic type, Roadmap project, Priority, Golden Pounds, and Target date fields without inventing taxonomy.
Does not derive Target date from Golden Pounds or sum child estimates without an explicit repository rule.
Verifies the final parent, children, dependencies, project fields, and issue fields from the remote.

output_evals.prompt: Create an epic-like parent for the checkout modernization. This GitHub org has no Epic issue type but uses parent issues and sub-issues in Roadmap.
assertions: Does not create a new Epic issue type or label merely to satisfy the request.
Uses the existing parent/sub-issue convention as the native epic representation.
Adds the parent to Roadmap using existing fields and options.
Keeps implementation-level detail in child issues and the integrated outcome in the parent.
Verifies hierarchy and project metadata after mutation.

output_evals.prompt: Create a GitLab epic for migrating all customer exports to the new pipeline. Use existing issues as children, preserve inherited start/due dates, and model blockers between work items.
assertions: Treats the Epic as a current GitLab work item and avoids building new automation around the deprecated legacy Epics REST API.
Inspects target instance/version/tier and CLI capabilities before choosing glab or Work Item API operations.
Preserves inherited dates instead of replacing them with guessed fixed dates.
Uses native child-item and linked-item relationships.
Models blockers on the work items that actually depend on each other, not only on the parent epic.
Verifies hierarchy, dates, and linked-item relationships from the remote.

output_evals.prompt: Draft an extremely complete epic for passwordless authentication across web, mobile, API, recovery, observability, and rollout, but do not create remote items.
assertions: Does not mutate the remote.
Defines one coherent outcome and explicit non-goals.
Includes security/privacy, compatibility, rollout, observability, risks, success signals, sequencing, and epic acceptance criteria.
Proposes independently verifiable child deliverables and identifies which would be issues versus nested epics.
Keeps child implementation details out of the epic-level acceptance criteria.
Returns proposed metadata and unresolved planning decisions separately.

output_evals.prompt: Create an epic for changing one API timeout constant and adding its regression test.
assertions: Recognizes the work as issue-sized rather than forcing an epic.
Does not manufacture child workstreams solely to make the request look epic-sized.
Redirects the work toward an implementation-ready issue while preserving the requested outcome.

output_evals.prompt: Create the epic and children even if one optional health or project field cannot be applied.
assertions: Creates the epic when core creation and hierarchy are possible.
Continues applying independent metadata and relationships after an optional field fails.
Does not silently drop the failed field.
Reports only the exact unapplied metadata and reason after verifying final remote state.
